analysis.title: $545 Billion Of AI Project Finance On Deck Next Year... But $320 Billion Of It Needs A Guarantor Who Just Left The Building
key_insights: Goldman's credit team raised its 2027 AI project finance forecast to $545B from $300B: $225B for data center shells and $320B for compute (GPUs and custom chips). 2026 year-to-date is $150B ($80B IG and junk data center bonds, $22B non-syndicated construction financing, $48B chip deals).

Compute financing would grow almost sevenfold from $48B year-to-date, while shell financing roughly doubles. Goldman's methodology assumes shells cost about $12M per megawatt in the US and chips about $25M per megawatt (about 1.7x the shell cost), with 45-50% of shells financed and 30% of compute for hyperscaler projects (45% for others).

Goldman's equity analysts expect 113 GW of compute to ship through 2028, while the credit team finds only 80 GW of data center capacity. Zero Hedge computes 113 GW at $25M per MW as roughly $2.8T of silicon, a third of it without obvious capacity.

Chip financings use a bankruptcy-remote SPV that owns the GPUs, with lenders repaid from a customer lease or compute service contract of five years or less. Goldman prefers equipment leases and the narrowest service contracts. Debt amortizes and the lease runs at least as long as the loan, so lenders rely on tenant credit and not on chip residual values.

Weaker chip deals lean on residual value guarantees from chipmakers, which in most deals cover close to the remaining principal and interest. IG chip deals priced at roughly 150-240bps new-issue spreads versus about 100bps for ordinary 5-7 year IG. The most recent leveraged finance print is near 775bps, about three times the going BB/B rate.

Goldman warns rating agencies have alluded to compounding left-tail exposure from guarantees that extend years beyond revenue recognition. Zero Hedge counts $530B of Nvidia commitments and guarantees at end of July from the 10-Q, including the $105B backstop of OpenAI's Ohio leases. BofA estimates about $230B of Nvidia financial guarantees as of August.

Chipmaker CDS trades about 75bps wide of their cash bonds, up from below zero a year ago, versus about 45bps for hyperscalers. Chipmakers have issued under $35B and have $94B of index-eligible bonds outstanding between them. Goldman expects the gap to keep widening. The chart ends Nov 12.

Per the WSJ, interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress is expected to rein in backstops, leases, buy-backs and startup investments. Nvidia's $500B chip-financing platform (launched in August with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, KKR and Goldman) offered residual value support on up to 25% of each deal and has closed zero deals because lenders want more cover. Broadcom backstopped $30B of a $35B Anthropic TPU deal in May and about 72.5% of a $63B deal.

Zero Hedge's math: at 25% cover, $320B of chip financing needs $80B of guarantees. At Broadcom's terms it needs $230B-$275B. This compares with $94B of index-eligible bonds outstanding from Nvidia, Broadcom and AMD combined. UBS's Tim Arcuri said a temporary pause in Nvidia dealmaking could pull $50B or more out of the AI ecosystem.

Reuters quotes: JPMorgan's Erica Spear expects existing commitments to stand but new deals to take longer or cost more. Morgan Stanley's Joseph Moore expects the $500B of third-party capital to go mostly to established players, mainly larger hyperscalers. PGIM's Edwin Wilches says lenders want future financings backed by customer contracts or financial guarantees.

Chip leases land in the 3-7 year part of the curve, where 60% of non-financial IG issuers and 40% of dollars raised sit. Goldman expects contained spillover for now because structured deals are not index-eligible, buyers need in-house expertise to analyze leases and draw schedules, and concentration limits apply. Zero Hedge notes this means a narrow buyer base.

Goldman expects more supply at the front end to flatten AI issuer curves, while guarantees stretching years out should keep long-end spreads from rallying much. Goldman expects this tension to come into focus around renewed volatility in AI spending outlook.

Shell financing: mutual funds and ETFs are underweight 13 of 16 HY data center bonds Goldman tracks, average active weight -0.07%. IG data center deals are outside the US Aggregate and US Corporate indices. Agg-benchmarked funds hold about a quarter of each deal and insurers about 10%.

Data center bond yields were 6-8% in the first half and the latest junk deals priced at 8-10%. In Goldman's illustrative project (90% loan-to-cost, 8% coupon, 1.2x debt service coverage), yield-on-cost must rise 1.4 points at a 9% coupon and 2.7 points at 10% to keep coverage. Where tenants resist, Goldman expects lower leverage via more equity, lower LTCs or tighter structures.

Goldman advocates a patient, selective approach to data center credit: underwrite on project specifics, since broad macro and technical beta is likely to drive spreads wider but not meaningfully tighter.

Hyperscalers sold $295B of bonds globally this year, exceeding Goldman's full-year forecast two months early, and now account for nearly $450B of the dollar IG index. Goldman says saturation limits how much higher-rated issuers can place in corporate credit, so more capex will be funded through structured financings at wider spreads.

Zero Hedge's view: the shell half likely gets financed at a price, while the compute half needs a new balance sheet: Nvidia reopening its guarantee window, hyperscalers taking chips onto their own balance sheets, or government support. Kress reports earnings today after the close.

market_movers.rationale: Interim CEO Kress is expected to rein in backstops and customer financing, and the $500B financing platform has closed zero deals at a 25% guarantee. Zero Hedge counts $530B of commitments and guarantees as of July, and BofA estimates about $230B of financial guarantees as of August.

Broadcom backstopped $30B of a $35B Anthropic TPU deal in May and about 72.5% of a $63B deal, offering better terms than Nvidia's 25% cover. Zero Hedge says Broadcom and AMD are among the few possible guarantors.

Named with Broadcom as one of few remaining possible guarantors for chip financing, and its bonds are part of the $94B of index-eligible chipmaker debt that would be asked to backstop $80B to $275B of guarantees.

sector_views.rationale: Goldman advocates a patient and selective approach, with spreads likely to be driven wider but not meaningfully tighter by macro and technical beta.
Zero Hedge argues the compute half of the forecast lacks a balance sheet now that Nvidia is stepping back from guarantees, with the chips possibly not getting bought.

earnings_insights: Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress is scheduled to report earnings today (Nov 18) after the close. Zero Hedge's question for the call is how many residual value guarantees she intends to sign.
Nvidia's last 10-Q (end of July) shows $530B of commitments and guarantees, including the $105B backstop of OpenAI's Ohio leases (Zero Hedge count).
risk_factors: Nvidia reduces residual value guarantees and customer financing just as lenders ask for more cover, leaving the compute half of the 2027 forecast without a guarantor.
Compounding left-tail guarantee exposure at chipmakers could draw rating agency action, as guarantees extend years beyond revenue recognition.
Fast chip obsolescence and uncertain residual values mean lenders depend on tenant credit, and neocloud and lower-rated borrowers cannot use their own balance sheets.
Higher coupons (8-10%) force tenants to pay higher rents or developers to use lower leverage, which shrinks debt per project.
Construction delays, tighter deal economics and data center moratoria, with tighter economics already slowing issuance this quarter and unsold deals building a backlog.
A narrow buyer base for structured chip debt (off-index, needs structured credit expertise, concentration limits).
Chip debt landing in the 3-7 year part of the curve could pressure spreads for industrial IG issuers if supply grows.
charts_described: Goldman chart shows AI project finance issuance on a broader global count rising from $77 billion in 2025 to $225 billion in 2026, then more than doubling in 2027.
Goldman chart shows the premium of chipmaker CDS over cash bonds rising from below zero a year ago to about 75bps, versus about 45bps for hyperscalers, ending Nov 12.
vol_and_positioning: Chipmaker CDS premium over cash bonds is about 75bps versus about 45bps for hyperscalers, up from below zero a year ago. The chart stops Nov 12, so the gap is probably wider now.

Mutual funds and ETFs are underweight 13 of 16 HY data center bonds with an average active weight of -0.07%. Agg-benchmarked funds hold about a quarter of each IG data center deal and insurers about 10%.
Most recent leveraged finance chip print is near 775bps, about three times the going rate for BB/B credit.
geopolitical: Zero Hedge says the Treasury Secretary is telling Nvidia's board whom to hire and the administration is reportedly preparing to name national AI champions, which it sees as a possible source of a new balance sheet for chip financing.
The governor-elect of Texas and similar officials in Georgia, Ohio and Michigan may push data center moratoria that Goldman's economists expect to be conditional and fade over time.
cross_bank_references: JPMorgan's Erica Spear expects existing Nvidia commitments to stand but new deals to take longer or require more compensation.
Morgan Stanley's Joseph Moore thinks the $500B of third-party capital is more likely to go to established players, mostly larger hyperscalers.
Bank of America estimates Nvidia had extended about $230 billion of financial guarantees as of August.
UBS's Tim Arcuri said even a temporary pause in Nvidia's dealmaking could pull $50 billion or more out of the AI ecosystem.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman sees $320B of compute financing in 2027 because capex is committed, the corporate bond market is saturated, and funding has to come from structured deals. Shell financing ($225B) likely clears at a price, as shown by Blackstone's deal with Amazon.
tension_points.bear_case: Lenders want more guarantee at the moment Nvidia is offering less, the $500B platform has closed zero deals at 25% cover, and the guarantees needed ($80B to $275B) dwarf the $94B of index-eligible chipmaker bonds. Higher coupons also force lower leverage on shells.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Kress's comments on Nvidia's earnings call today after the close on how many residual value guarantees Nvidia intends to sign, and whether Nvidia reopens its guarantee window.
